claims.claim: TXN identity and NASDAQ tradability are validated by the current promotion packet; reused primary evidence is issuer-originated and current Q2 2026 operating evidence is independently addressable from the issuer release and SEC proxy, while current valuation is separately sourced.

risks.risk: Current valuation is materially richer than year-end 2025 while the semiconductor cycle and utilization remain cyclical.

unknowns.unknown: Exact incremental returns on each new 300mm fab remain dependent on future utilization.

claims.claim: Q2 2026 revenue rose 23% year over year to $5.463B, operating profit rose 48%, and trailing-12-month free cash flow reached $6.534B as capex fell to $3.312B, supporting strong operating momentum while utilization cyclicality remains a material risk.

TXN's internally owned 300mm manufacturing footprint, broad analog/embedded portfolio and planned Silicon Labs acquisition support durable physical-system relevance and cross-market leverage, but the September 2026 valuation near 41.8x trailing earnings materially limits valuation headroom.

thesisQuality.basis: Broad analog/embedded demand, Q2 2026 broad growth and internally owned low-cost manufacturing support durable differentiation, tempered by semiconductor cyclicality.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q2 revenue +23% YoY, operating profit +48%, TTM CFO $8.667B and FCF $6.534B with materially lower capex.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: September 2026 trailing P/E near 41.8x versus 31.5x at year-end 2025 indicates demanding valuation despite improving earnings.

catalystScore.basis: Q3 revenue/EPS outlook implies continued recovery and the Silicon Labs transaction offers identifiable 2027 synergy/cross-sell catalysts, subject to closing.

governancePower.basis: Long-tenured internal CFO succession and explicit capital-allocation discipline support continuity; proxy confirms standard common-stock voting structure.

alignment2036.basis: Analog and embedded semiconductors are foundational sensing, power-management and control components across industrial, automotive and data-center physical systems.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Growth was broad across industrial, data center and automotive, while Silicon Labs adds wireless connectivity and cross-sell potential across the same manufacturing/channel base.

bottleneckControl.basis: Internal 300mm capacity and assembly/test provide cost and supply control, but analog supply remains competitively substitutable across many categories.

scenarioRobustness.basis: End-market breadth and modular capacity improve resilience, but industrial/automotive semiconductor demand remains cyclical and fixed-cost utilization matters.

substitutionResilience.basis: Broad catalog, embedded customer qualification and owned process/manufacturing capabilities raise replacement friction, while competing analog vendors remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: 2026 plan targets >90% internal wafers and >70% of internal wafers on 300mm, with >85% assembly internal, materially increasing internal supply control.

pricingPower.basis: Q2 operating profit grew 48% on 23% revenue growth and analog operating profit grew 50%, supporting strong incremental economics, though cycle sensitivity prevents exceptional scoring.

riskEvidence.basis: Principal risks are semiconductor-cycle relapse, underutilization of expanded fixed-cost capacity, rich valuation and execution/financing risk around the $7.5B Silicon Labs acquisition.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current issuer operating data, capital-management disclosures, SEC governance evidence and an independent current valuation source cover all score dimensions; exact future fab utilization and acquisition realization remain unknown.

scoreRecord.thesis: Texas Instruments combines broad analog/embedded exposure with increasingly internalized 300mm manufacturing, giving it durable relevance, cost/supply leverage and strong cash generation across physical-system electrification; the main offset is a demanding current valuation and cyclical utilization risk.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: A demand relapse could underutilize expanded manufacturing capacity while a rich valuation and Silicon Labs execution amplify downside sensitivity.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 operating results versus the $5.65B-$6.15B revenue outlook and progress toward the Silicon Labs transaction close in the first half of 2027.

risks.risk: Cyclical demand relapse can expose fixed-cost underutilization and compress returns.
The Silicon Labs transaction introduces financing, regulatory and integration risk.
Current valuation requires sustained execution and offers limited error tolerance.

unknowns.unknown: Future utilization and realized returns on each incremental fab are not yet observable.
Silicon Labs transaction synergies remain prospective until close and integration.
